issues.quote: Herrgott, the regulator on the wall had stopped. And he had his repeater in his hand.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the atelier regulator or the master's repeater, and says nothing about either clock having stopped or being read.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped wall regulator as a time-of-death or time-of-stopping clue, and the repeater as a watch whose reading matters. Neither is among the four readings, so either could lead the solver to a clock time the sheet never gives.

issues.quote: the master will want to see the new year come in with his watch in his hand
issues.fact: The sheet does not say the master was carrying a watch or planning to check the time at midnight.
issues.misreading: This implies a watch-checking habit at a set time, which a solver could read as a hint about when he was last alive or about when he would have looked at his watch.

issues.quote: So I went up the stairs to the atelier, and I opened the door, and he was on the floor.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no time for Rosa going upstairs or finding the master.
issues.misreading: Placing the trip upstairs right after the toast is ready suggests a timing or whereabouts that the sheet does not establish.
